newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana video poker revenues drop for first time.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana video poker revenues drop for first time.

text.p: Louisiana's video poker revenues totaled $783 million in the last six months of 1996, declining for the first time since the games were authorized five yeas ago, state police said.
The gross revenues, the total of money dropped into the machines, were down from $788 million in the first half of 1996.
Net revenues, after winners were paid but before taxes and other expenses, also dropped from $304 million in the first half of the year to $301 million in the second half.
Franchise fees, the portion of video poker revenues shared by state and local governments, dropped to $84.4 million in the last half of 1996 from $84.8 million in the first half.
Until now, video poker revenues had risen for every six months, compared to the previous six.

"This is to be expected, actually, to get a rapid growth for a while, followed by a slowing growth, a plateau and then possibly a little bit of decrease, particularly if you are having competition from other sources like expanding riverboats and Mississippi casinos," David Johnson, an economics professor at Louisiana State University, told the Advocate newspaper.
Industry officials said revenues may also be declining because players' skill levels are improving.
In November, 33 parishes voted to end video poker but existing outlets in those parishes will continue to operate until mid-1999.
